newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IFO business index falls in December.
newsitem.headline: German IFO business index falls in December.

text.p: Germany's respected Ifo economics institute said on Tuesday its west German business climate index fell sharply in December, reflecting worries that the economic recovery is not as robust as had been hoped.
The Munich-based institute said the west German climate index -- the most closely watched of Ifo's confidence barometers -- fell to 95.8 in December from November's 96.9.
The business conditions and business expectations measures also dropped -- to 89.8 and 101.8 respectively. In November the conditions index stood at 91.4 and expectations at 102.4.
For east Germany, the business climate dropped to 104.4 from 104.8 in November.
German Bund futures initially surged on the report although prices later dropped back sharply.
In the share market, the 30-share DAX dipped below the psychologically important 3,000-point level on the news. The index was down 46.69 points at 2,983.99 in midsession trade.
The economic data were worse than most economists had expected and some said it would increase pressure on the Bundesbank to lower interest rates further to stimulate growth.
Stefan Schneider, economist at Banque Paribas Capital Management in Frankfurt said that cold weather which had hurt construction had pushed the overall index lower.
"Pressure on the Bundesbank is increasing, also since the government finds itself in a straitjacket," he said.
But he added that he saw little prospect of a near-term interest rate cut to help the economy, adding that long-term yields, which are crucial for the German economy, were continuing to ease.
"The Bundesbank won't move soon. Bund yields could fall further in the short term. I believe 5.50 percent is possible," Schneider said.
Hans-Juergen Meltzer at Deutsche Bank agreed that special factors had hurt the index in December.
"There were two to three fewer working days (in December). That might explain the lower number," he said.

But he also saw no chance of an early Bundesbank easing, "For the time being there will not be a cut in the repo rate, but pressure may mount," he said, referring to the central bank's main money market rate, the securities repurchase rate.
